content.value_statement: AI agents fail when context grows noisy, stale, or too large for reliable attention. This skill explains practical context design patterns for better agent behavior.
actual_capabilities: Explains the main parts of model context: system prompts, tools, documents, message history, and tool outputs.
Describes progressive disclosure for skills, documents, and tool results.
Guides context budgeting, compaction planning, and attention-aware placement of critical information.
Shows how to organize system prompts with clear sections and direct instructions.
Covers filesystem-based access and hybrid context-loading strategies for agent systems.
limitations: Provides concepts and guidance, not executable automation.
Does not inspect a real application or measure token usage automatically.
Does not replace security review for prompts or tools that access private data.
Requires adaptation to each model, toolchain, and context window.

use_cases.title: Plan Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Use the skill to decide what context should load at startup and what should load on demand.

use_cases.title: Review Prompt Systems
use_cases.description: Use the skill to find bloated, vague, or poorly positioned context in existing agent prompts.

use_cases.title: Onboard AI Teams
use_cases.description: Use the skill as a shared foundation for explaining context windows, attention limits, and progressive disclosure.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Context Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the main parts of language model context for my team. Keep the explanation practical and include common failure modes.

prompt_templates.title: Assess My Agent Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent design for context quality. Identify what should be preloaded, retrieved on demand, compacted, or removed.

prompt_templates.title: Design Progressive Disclosure
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design progressive disclosure for this AI workflow. Separate startup context, referenced files, tool outputs, and fallback context.

prompt_templates.title: Create Context Budget Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a context budget strategy for a long-running agent. Include thresholds, compaction triggers, attention placement, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: I am designing an agent with large project documents and frequent tool calls.
output: Load project rules and tool guidance at startup.
Keep long documents behind stable references.
Retrieve only task-specific sections when needed.
Compact tool output when context usage reaches planned thresholds.

output_examples.input: My agent forgets requirements during long implementation tasks.
output: Place critical requirements near the beginning or end of context.
Summarize completed work before the context becomes crowded.
Remove low-signal logs and unrelated tool output.
Track unresolved decisions in a concise working note.

output_examples.input: I need to explain context engineering to new team members.
output_examples.output: Context is the active information a model can attend to. Good systems keep it small, relevant, current, and easy to navigate.

best_practices: Keep startup context small and reserve space for task-specific evidence.
Place critical constraints where the model is most likely to attend to them.
Use compaction and selective retrieval before long tasks exceed reliable context limits.
anti_patterns: Do not load every document at startup without a task-specific reason.
Do not rely on vague prompts when concrete tool or output guidance is needed.
Do not keep stale tool output in context after it stops supporting current decisions.

faq.question: What does this skill teach?
faq.answer: It teaches the core ideas behind context engineering for language models and AI agents.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands or scripts?
faq.answer: No. It is a documentation skill with examples and design guidance only.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when designing, debugging, reviewing, or teaching AI agent context systems.

faq.question: Does it apply to Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The context concepts apply across these tools, though implementation details may differ.

faq.question: Can it optimize context automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains strategies you can apply when designing or reviewing an agent workflow.

faq.question: What should I read next?
faq.answer: Read related material on context degradation, context optimization, multi-agent patterns, and tool design.
